answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x during daily settlement peak with heavy writes; the objective is sustained availability without dropping customer writes. memory_b3 is the closest load-peak analogue (headroom kept queues flat). memory_b5 recovered write latency by shedding read/dashboard load, so it is worth confirming whether mixed primary load is in play; if the pain is the writes themselves, replicas will not help. Not choosing enable_circuit_breaker: memory_b4 contained a partner outage by failing fast, which would lose settlement writes. Not choosing rollback yet: memory_b1 cleared an error spike after a bad build, but today we have latency rather than reported checkout errors, and the release/peak timing still confounds. Failover remains unindicated without a regional signature. Verify b3 and b5, then add a small guarded increment of write capacity so peak settlement can continue.
